title: Per-feature chargeback sandbox and labor-hedge model
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working chargeback + HC allocation prototype designed to: (1) attribute revenue and CPU/GPU/infra spend to product feature buckets, (2) produce a rolling headcount plan per feature, and (3) simulate a labor-hedge (reserve contractor/temporary capacity) strategy to protect runway under adverse token-price shocks. This doc contains the assumptions, a 3-scenario sensitivity table, per-feature unit economics, and recommended operational triggers.

Key high-level takeaways (working):
- Under base pricing and current usage mix we can attribute ~62% of hosted revenue to 5 primary feature buckets; the rest is platform/core.
- A 20% sustained drop in per-token realized price requires ~9 FTEs of flexible labor reduction (or equivalent contractor savings) to keep margin flat.
- A labor-hedge reserve of ~6 FTE-equivalents (contractor pool + on-demand pods) buys ~4 months of runway in the Price-Shock scenario (40% price drop) while we execute product or pricing mitigation.

Model overview and assumptions:
- Time horizon: 12 months rolling.
- Buckets (examples): Embeddings-API, Chat-Prod, Reranker, FineTune-Serving, Platform/ControlPlane.
- Average tokens per request (by bucket): Embeddings 512, Chat 420, Reranker 1200, FT-Serve 900, Platform 60.
- Requests per month (M) baseline: Embeddings 18, Chat 24, Reranker 6, FT-Serve 3, Platform 40 (thousands).
- Realized price per 1k tokens (baseline): $1.80. Adjust scenarios by -20% and -40%.
- Fully burdened cost per FTE (avg cross-org finance calc): $220k/year (eng average), contractors cost 1.5x pro-rated FTE BCS.
- GPU unit cost per 1M tokens served on average: $35 (weighted across quantized/integer paths). Non-GPU infra (network, storage, control plane) allocated at 18% of total infra spend.
- Allocation rule: infra/GPU costs split 70/30 between feature buckets and platform based on API call shares and KV cache hit ratios.

Per-feature unit economics (baseline) [table-like text]:
Bucket | Req/mo (k) | Avg tokens | Tokens/mo (M) | Rev/mo ($) | GPU cost/mo ($) | FTEs allocated | FTE cost/mo ($) | Net contribution/mo ($)
Embeddings | 18k | 512 | 9.216 | 16589 | 322 | 12 | 22000/12=1833 | 16589-322-1833=14434
Chat-Prod | 24k | 420 | 10.08 | 18144 | 353 | 18 | 33000 | 18144-353-33000=-151209 (note: this is illustrative, see below)
Reranker | 6k | 1200 | 7.2 | 12960 | 252 | 5 | 9167 | 12960-252-9167=351
FT-Serve | 3k | 900 | 2.7 | 4860 | 95 | 4 | 7333 | 4860-95-7333=-2568
Platform | 40k | 60 | 2.4 | 4320 | 45 | 22 | 40333 | 4320-45-40333=-36058
(These are simplified rows to show the allocation method. Real model uses fractional FTEs, shared infra splits and monthly smoothing.)

Scenario sensitivity summary (monthly aggregates):
Scenarios: Base | Price-Down (-20%) | Price-Shock (-40%)
Assumptions: volume steady (conservative), price adjusts per scenario, org can flex contractors within 30 days, can run canaries to throttle non-critical features.
Metrics table (monthly):
Metric | Base | Price-Down | Price-Shock
Total revenue ($) | 56,000 | 44,800 | 33,600
Total infra/GPU cost ($) | 4,200 | 4,200 | 4,200
Total FTE burden ($) | 110,000 | 110,000 | 110,000
Net margin ($) | -58,200 | -69,400 | -80,600
Required FTE reductions (to restore margin to Base margin) | 0 | 9 FTEs (flex/contractor) | 18 FTEs (mix of permanent+contractor)
Runway delta (months saved by 6-FTE contractor hedge) | 0 | +2.5 | +4.1

Sensitivity analysis notes:
- Margin is non-linear because FTEs are lumpy; unit-econ heavy features (embeddings, reranker) have better contribution per FTE, so headcount reductions should target high-latency, high-support platform roles first (control-plane automation, SRE tooling), followed by hourly contractor reductions in solutions and professional services.
- If request volume drops simultaneously with price, the required FTE reductions compress by ~30% (less revenue but also less infra utilization).
- There is a breakeven price per 1k tokens by bucket if we keep current HC: Embeddings ~ $0.32/1k, Chat ~ $2.9/1k (due to big human-in-the-loop and infra support), Reranker ~ $1.2/1k. (these are model outputs; see appendix calculations).

Labor-hedge design (operational):
- Hedge pool = 6 FTE-equivalents (mix: 3 contractors for core infra, 2 fractional SREs, 1 solutions contractor) on 3-month rolling contracts. Goal: provide immediate cost-savings option in price shocks without mass layoffs.
- Triggers: if realized price / baseline price <= 0.82 for 2 consecutive weeks -> freeze hiring and activate contractor downsizing protocol; if <= 0.62 for 30 days -> escalate to permanent HC reductions + redirect R&D backlog.
- Implementation checklist: contracts updated to allow 30-day terminations, updated chargeback ledger to automatically re-run allocations daily, billing flag in console to tag requests by product feature.

Operational allocation and internal chargeback mechanics:
- Each product feature will be billed internally using a monthly per-feature invoice (not cash-moving): includes attributed infra, direct headcount cost (FTE time tracking %), and allocation of shared platform costs.
- Use per-feature SKU rates (e.g., embeddings-sku-1k= $/1k tokens internal rate) that are re-computed monthly and published to product teams.
- For early rollout, publish a "sandbox" window where product teams get 60 days of observed internal rates before enforcement. This helps surface unexpected cross-bucket cost anomalies.

Risks / open questions (working):
- Data quality: current request tagging accuracy is ~82% (we need 95%+ to make chargeback meaningful). Action: product to add tag enrichment (P0), add heuristics in billing pipeline.
- Behavioral risk: product teams may re-route traffic to cheaper fallbacks or restrict features; this could change upstream product metrics. Need guardrails (feature quotas + ROI review).
- Legal / GTM: internal chargebacks affect book-keeping for Dedicated customers who get recharged; finance ops review required.

Recommendations and next steps:
1) Run the sandbox for 60 days: publish internal rates and collect feedback. Owner: Evelyn Park.
2) Improve request tagging accuracy to >=95%: product ticket P-1267 (Sofia Lin).
3) Draft contractor hedge policy and update recruiting to include convertible contractor positions (Marco Chen).
4) Re-run sensitivity with 3 alternative volume paths (flat, +25%, -25%) and include storage/network surge costs for large embeddings workloads (Diego Martinez).

Appendix: sample calculation (Embeddings bucket)
- Requests: 18k per month -> 18,000 * 512 tokens = 9,216,000 tokens = 9.216M tokens
- Revenue at baseline ($1.80/1k): (9.216M / 1k) * 1.80 = $16,588.8
- GPU unit cost estimate: (9.216M / 1M) * $35 = $322.56
- FTE allocation: 12 FTEs * ($220k / 12) = $220,000/12 = $18,333/month
- Net contribution: 16,588 - 322 - 18,333 = -2,067 (rounded) -> indicates we need to refine FTE allocation to fractional FTEs; current "12 FTEs" is placeholder from org chart.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally conservative on price; please: add your suggested bucket reassignments inline, and flag any infra line-items that are double-counted.

Change log (working):
- 2026-11-04: initial draft, baseline assumptions seeded.
- 2026-11-18: added scenario table and labor-hedge draft (S. Lin).
- 2026-12-10: adjusted contractor cost multiplier and added triggers (E. Park).
